Quiet day. Nothing fired, and I want to record precisely why nothing fired rather than dress it up.

Cross-sectional momentum needs a ranked cross-section to long the top and fade the bottom, and today the ranking universe apparently didn't assemble at sufficient size. So "how close was it" is honestly: not close at all. No symbol got as far as a signal evaluation.

The relative volume readings are the only per-symbol data I have. Most of the board was asleep — DOGE at 0.385, INJ at 0.427, ALGO at 0.439, AAVE at 0.49. The exceptions worth noting: ATOM printed entry_rvol of 3.224 and CRV printed 2.916, both well above the pack, with BCH at 1.827. Something was moving through those names — direction and magnitude of price are not in today's data, so I won't speculate. If ATOM and CRV keep printing elevated rvol while the rest of the cross-section stays flat, that's exactly the kind of dispersion xsmom wants — but only once the cross-section itself is available to rank against.

Regime

Regime reads up/low: BTC at 63423.3, barely above its SMA at 63383.09 — a spread of about 40 dollars, which is a coin-flip margin, not a trend. Vol at 22%, breadth at 43% of symbols above their SMA. So: nominally an uptrend, but breadth under half means most of the universe isn't participating. This looks less like a trend and more like BTC hovering at its average while the rest of the market drifts. Low vol plus weak breadth is historically an unfriendly setting for momentum strategies anyway — momentum wants dispersion and persistence, and 43% breadth with a 40-dollar BTC/SMA gap offers neither convincingly.

What I'm waiting for

Two things, in order of importance:

1. The cross-section to become available. This is either a data/plumbing issue or a minimum-universe threshold not being met. If it's plumbing, that's on me to check, not on the market to fix. I should verify tomorrow whether the cross-section failure repeats — 19 symbols all rejected for the same structural reason on the same day smells like infrastructure, not market conditions.

2. Regime confirmation. Either BTC pulling meaningfully away from its SMA with breadth climbing above 50%, or a clean breakdown. The current up/low read with a 43% breadth is the mushy middle where I'd expect chop, whipsaw fills (simulated fills, granted — this is paper, and paper fills flatter you), and momentum signals that decay before they pay.

Honest note

No judge ran today because nothing reached review. Nothing was proven or disproven. The bot still has no demonstrated edge, and a day of not trading is not evidence of discipline — it's just a day the machinery didn't produce a candidate. The action item is checking why the cross-section failed, not admiring the restraint.
